Indication to ICD.summary: Based on sudden cardiac death risk models. Consider ICD implantation if family history of sudden cardiac death in one or more first-degree relatives under 40 years of age or sudden cardiac death in a first-degree relative with confirmed HCM at any age; NSVT; unexplained syncope.
notes: Family history of sudden cardiac death in first-degree relatives <40 years or in a first-degree relative with confirmed HCM at any age

Fabry disease.summary: Mentioned with reference to treatment: enzyme replacement therapy for alpha-galactosidase A deficiency.

Amyloidosis.summary: Referred to; cross-reference to section 14.6 and figure 21 for details.

Definition (HCM).summary: Wall thickness >14 mm in one or more LV myocardial segments not explained solely by abnormal loading conditions. LVOTO ≥30 mmHg at rest or exercise, asymmetric hypertrophy, or increased LGE in a patchy mid-wall pattern supports HCM. Familial when two or more first- or second-degree relatives with HCM or a first-degree relative with autopsy-proven HCM and sudden death <50 years are detected.

Differential diagnosis.summary: Distinguish HCM from physiological hypertrophy (athletic training), severe hypertension, aortic stenosis, isolated septal hypertrophy; consider genetic HCM if disproportionate. Consider amyloidosis when increased thickness of interatrial septum, AV valve or RV free wall detected.

Genetic counselling and testing.Indication: Must be offered to all patients with a diagnosis of HCM to identify a possible underlying genetic cause and to all first-degree adult relatives of patients with HCM and a definite disease-causing mutation, regardless of phenotype.
Genetic counselling and testing.Family screening: Clinical evaluation, ECG and echocardiography must be performed in first-degree relatives who have the same definite disease-causing mutation as the index patient.
